newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic children's pacemaker lead okayed.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic children's pacemaker lead okayed.

text.p: Medtronic Inc said Tuesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved for commercial release a new pacemaker lead for infants and children.

Medtronic said its Model 4965 steroid-eluting lead has been tested since 1989 in infants and children, most of whom have undergone complex surgical procedures to repair congenital heart defects and need implanted pacemakers.

Pacemaker leads are insulated wires that transmit electrical impulses from the pacemaker to the heart. Medtronic said its new lead is designed to be attached to the exterior heart wall in a gentler way than earlier leads.
Medtronic said Model 4965 can be fixed in place with sutures and incorporates a steroid-eluting electrode that minimizes inflammation at its contact point.
The new lead is available in lengths as short as 10 inches, as well as longer lengths. Most pacemaker leads for adults are about 22 inches long, Medtronic said.
